exam.title: JSE Certified Entry-Level JavaScript Programmer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite is published. Practice predicting, running, testing, and debugging small browser-based JavaScript programs across runtime boundaries, declarations/scope/hoisting, primitive and reference values, conversions/operators/dialogs, conditionals/loops, first-class functions/recursion/timer callbacks, and errors/exceptions. Keep host APIs separate from the core language and verify the active version before purchase.

Three browser scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks are included. The scope page remains the objective authority; 8/20/18/21/21/12 is labeled as the official practice kit's content distribution rather than silently presented as main-syllabus weighting. findings.title: Canonical exam scope and practice distribution differ
findings.evidence: The full canonical page has 30 bullets in six blocks without percentage weights; the separate practice kit lists a content distribution.
findings.recommendation: Remove percentages from domain headings, preserve explicitly labeled practice distribution and map all 30 scope bullets, excluding the holder profile.
findings.resolution: Remove percentages from domain headings, preserve explicitly labeled practice distribution and map all 30 scope bullets, excluding the holder profile.

findings.title: Cancellation and blank text must precede numeric conversion
findings.evidence: Prompt returns null for cancellation and an empty string for accepted empty input. Number conversion alone can turn either into zero.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit bounded decimal-text contract and execute cancellation, blank, malformed, boundary and valid-zero dialog paths.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit bounded decimal-text contract and execute cancellation, blank, malformed, boundary and valid-zero dialog paths.

findings.title: Global lexical bindings are not global-object properties
findings.evidence: Top-level let differs from classic-script var; modules introduce another scope boundary. typeof also does not bypass temporal dead zones.
findings.recommendation: Add precise scope prose, classic/module probes and executed typeof/hoisting checks.
findings.resolution: Add precise scope prose, classic/module probes and executed typeof/hoisting checks.

findings.title: Safe integers and BigInt conversion need operation-specific rules
findings.evidence: Larger Number values may lose adjacent integer distinctions; explicit BigInt inputs have different error classes.
findings.recommendation: Add exact text conversion, unsafe integer collision and RangeError/SyntaxError/TypeError comparisons in the original workbook.
findings.resolution: Add exact text conversion, unsafe integer collision and RangeError/SyntaxError/TypeError comparisons in the original workbook.

findings.title: Timer scheduling is not a guaranteed clock
findings.evidence: Callback scheduling can be delayed; a scheduling try does not enclose later callback execution.
findings.recommendation: Complete a bounded timer state machine with cleanup, restart and late-answer tests, and capture an actual later callback page error.
findings.resolution: Complete a bounded timer state machine with cleanup, restart and late-answer tests, and capture an actual later callback page error.

findings.title: Paused state changes do not repair source code
findings.evidence: Debugging tutorial distinguishes variable inspection/change from correcting the original source.
findings.recommendation: Execute an original paused/stepped local probe, alter a local before arithmetic, rerun unchanged code and verify the source correction separately.
findings.resolution: Execute an original paused/stepped local probe, alter a local before arithmetic, rerun unchanged code and verify the source correction separately.

groups.title: Exam block #1: Introduction to JavaScript and Computer Programming
objectives: understand the fundamental programming concepts, such as: interpreting and the interpreter, compilation and the compiler, client-side vs. server-side programming;
have a basic knowledge of how to set up and use a basic programming environment (online or local)
gain skills allowing them to run their first JavaScript program on the client side (both as an element embedded in the HTML page and directly in the browser console).

groups.title: Exam block #2: Variable, Data Types, and Type Casting
objectives: have the knowledge and skills to work with variables, i.e. naming, declaring, initializing and modifying their values;
understand concepts such as scope, code blocks, shadowing, hoisting;
know the basic properties of primitive data types such as boolean, number, bigint, undefined, null, and be able to use them;
be familiar with the basic properties of the primitive data type string, including string literals – single or double quotes, escape character, string interpolation, basic properties and methods;
know the basic properties of complex data types such as Array and Object (treated as a record) and be able to use them in practice.

groups.title: Exam block #3: Operators and User Interaction
objectives: know what operators are and how we classify them (by type of operands, by number of operands, etc.)
be able to use assignment, arithmetic, logical, and comparison operators in practice;
have an understanding of the operation of the conditional operator and the typeof, instanceof, and delete operators;
understand what the precedence and associativity of basic operators are and be able to influence it by means of bracket grouping;
be able to perform basic two-way communication with the program user using the alert, confirm, and prompt dialog boxes.

groups.title: Exam block #4: Control Flow – Conditional Execution and Loops
objectives: be able to force conditional execution of a group of statements (make decisions and branch the flow) using if-else and switch commands;
be able to force a group of statements to repeat in a loop using the for, while, and do-while commands, using both dependent and independent conditions on the number of iterations;
understand and be able to use loop-specific break and continue instructions;
be able to use the for-in statement to iterate over properties of an object;
be able to use the for-of statement to walk through the elements of an array.

groups.title: Exam block #5: Functions
objectives: be able to declare and call functions;
know how to pass call arguments to a function and return the result of its operation from it;
understand the concept of a local variable and the effect of shadowing variables with the same names within a function;

know that a function in JS is a first-class member and be able to take advantage of this by declaring functions using function expression and passing functions as arguments to calls of other functions;
understand the concept of recursion in the context of functions and be able to solve simple programming problems by using it;
have a basic understanding of the callback function and be able to use it asynchronously in conjunction with the setTimeout and setInterval methods;
have a clear understanding of arrow function notation and be able to write functions alternatively as a regular declaration, a function expression, and an arrow function.

groups.title: Exam block #6: Errors, exceptions, debugging, and troubleshooting
objectives: understand the differences between syntactic, semantic, and logical errors;
understand the concept of an exception and distinguish between the basic exceptions generated by JS when an error occurs: SyntaxError, ReferenceError, TypeError, RangeError;
have the ability to handle exceptions using the try-catch-finally statement;
be able to generate their own exceptions using the throw statement;
have the skills to use the debugger for basic analysis of their own code, including: step-by-step execution, viewing and modifying variables, and measuring code execution time.
